subject: pathology
title: Non neoplastic CNS disease: stroke, MS, meningitis and prions

steps.tx: Ischaemic stroke syndromes localise accurately from the pattern of neurological deficit. A **middle cerebral artery stroke** causes contralateral face and arm weakness, and **intravenous thrombolysis** is given within the stated window after bleeding is excluded. Large vessel occlusion can require thrombectomy, and glucose is checked first because hypoglycaemia mimics stroke closely.
steps.say: Stroke localisation is determined by the pattern of weakness and language deficit. The middle cerebral artery causes face and arm weakness with aphasia commonly. Bleeding is excluded by imaging before thrombolysis is given to eligible patients. Glucose is checked first because hypoglycaemia mimics stroke very closely.

steps.tx: Subarachnoid haemorrhage presents suddenly with the worst headache of life. A ruptured **berry aneurysm** causes thunderclap headache, and **xanthochromia** in cerebrospinal fluid confirms bleeding when imaging is negative. Vasospasm develops days later and nimodipine is used, whereas rebleeding and hydrocephalus are other major early complications.
steps.say: Subarachnoid bleeding presents with thunderclap headache and vomiting very suddenly. A berry aneurysm ruptures at a bifurcation and blood fills basal cisterns. Xanthochromia confirms bleeding when the initial scan is negative in suspected cases. Vasospasm develops later and nimodipine is used for prevention.

steps.tx: This axial CT shows bright blood filling the basal cisterns around the midbrain. **Subarachnoid blood** appears hyperdense on non contrast imaging, and the **basal cisterns** are the key place to inspect after thunderclap headache. This pattern matters because it confirms aneurysmal bleeding and triggers urgent vascular imaging and neurosurgical referral.
steps.say: This scan is abnormal because bright blood is present in basal cisterns. Blood is hyperdense on non contrast CT and it outlines the cisterns clearly. This pattern confirms subarachnoid haemorrhage in the correct clinical setting rapidly. Urgent vascular imaging is required because an aneurysm requires treatment.

vis.alt: Axial noncontrast head CT showing bright subarachnoid blood filling basal cisterns around midbrain.
vis.caption: Axial brain CT showing hyperdense blood in basal cisterns. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Multiple sclerosis is an autoimmune demyelinating disease of young adults. **Multiple sclerosis** produces periventricular plaques and **Dawson fingers** on imaging, and internuclear ophthalmoplegia results from a medial longitudinal fasciculus lesion. Oligoclonal bands support the diagnosis, and relapses are treated with pulsed steroids while disease modifying drugs reduce future relapses.
steps.say: Multiple sclerosis is autoimmune and it demyelinates central white matter tracts progressively. Periventricular plaques are characteristic and Dawson fingers extend from the ventricles outward. Internuclear ophthalmoplegia occurs because the medial longitudinal fasciculus is demyelinated focally. Oligoclonal bands support diagnosis because intrathecal antibody production is present.

steps.tx: Cerebrospinal fluid patterns separate bacterial, viral and tuberculous meningitis rapidly. Bacterial meningitis shows **neutrophilic fluid** with low glucose, and tuberculous meningitis shows **basal exudates** with cranial nerve palsies. Normal pressure hydrocephalus causes gait disturbance, incontinence and cognitive decline, and Creutzfeldt Jakob disease causes rapid dementia with myoclonus.
steps.say: Bacterial fluid is neutrophilic and glucose is low with high protein levels. Viral fluid is lymphocytic and glucose remains normal in most cases typically. Tuberculous disease causes basal exudates and cranial nerve palsies over weeks. Normal pressure hydrocephalus is reversible because shunting improves gait in selected patients.
